groundwaterLevels.parameterMeaning: Water level, depth LSD - depth to water level, feet below land surface (confirmed via parameter-codes/items)
groundwaterLevels.gives: Individual field-visit depth-to-water readings per well, fit to a simple linear trend (ordinary least squares, ft/year) over the well's full qualifying record.
groundwaterLevels.note: Legacy waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/gwlevels/ is decommissioned (confirmed: now 301s to USGS's own decommission notice); this uses the replacement OGC API at api.waterdata.usgs.gov, live-verified 2026-08-27.
groundwaterLevels.qualifyingWellRule: A well qualifies as a county's representative only with a field-measurements-metadata span >= 15 years AND a most-recent reading within the last 10 years (not an abandoned well from decades ago), AND >= 6 usable readings after the full history was actually fetched. 1330 counties nationally have a qualifying well out of 3222 total - this uneven coverage is real, not a bug: candidates.json flagged it in advance ("monitoring-well density is genuinely uneven").
groundwaterLevels.oneWellPerCounty: Exactly one representative well (longest qualifying span, ties broken by most recent) stands in for the whole county. This is a real simplification - a single well is not the whole county's aquifer - and every page must say so, the same way FloodZoneCheck's pages disclose parcel-vs-county granularity.
groundwaterLevels.trendMethod: Ordinary least-squares linear regression of depth-to-water (ft below land surface) against time (years) across every usable reading in the well's qualifying record. Positive slope = getting deeper = water table declining. decline_10yr_ft/decline_30yr_ft are the slope extrapolated forward, not a measured 10/30-year change for wells with a shorter or longer actual record - the model/template layer must present this as a rate-based projection, not a guarantee.

gazetteer.gives: county FIPS, name, state, lat/lon, land area

joinMethod: Numeric FIPS join throughout: USGS state_code (2-digit) + county_code (3-digit) = the same 5-digit FIPS the Census Gazetteer and population files use. No name-matching, unlike RadonZoneCheck's EPA-sheet join.
